primary_claim: Simple LLM 'diffing agents' that craft their own prompts to compare two models reliably discover valid, systematic behavioural differences between real model pairs (e.g. Gemini 2.5 Pro vs 3 Pro), achieve a low false-positive rate when the two models are identical, and outperform single-model auditing agents at finding subtle conditional behavioural differences in model organisms -- though they fail to find the intended secret behaviour in a finetuned model organism, which the authors attribute to a failure of the model organism (too many other salient side-effect differences) rather than the diffing method.

effect.metric: ground-truth score (trigger + behaviour identification, 0-100%) on system-prompted model organisms, diffing agent vs single-model auditing baseline
effect.value: diffing agent almost always outperforms the single-model auditing baseline on the subtle-behaviour evaluation set

contradicts_or_qualifies: Extends prior black-box behavioural model-diffing work (Dunlap et al. 2024, Kempf et al. 2026) by having an auditor agent craft its own prompts rather than compare on a fixed static prompt distribution

Qualifies the usefulness of the Cywiński et al. (2025) Gemma-2-9b user-gender model organism as a ground-truth benchmark: the diffing agent finds several true behavioural differences but never the intended user-gender behaviour, suggesting the model organism has other, more salient, side effects
stated_future_work: separate hypothesis generation and validation into distinct agent trajectories to reduce false positive rates
establish more evaluations with known ground-truth differences for evaluating diffing agents

optimize diffing methods to solve a real problem, e.g. build a model organism with secret knowledge that behaves as similarly as possible to its base model using diffing tools in the optimization pipeline
find and fix a real alignment-relevant behaviour in a model discovered by a diffing pipeline
use model diffing tools within the model-organism creation pipeline to better control unintended side effects
limitations_stated: conditional system-instruction model organisms aren't perfect: even when the trigger fires, the model may have other valid behavioural differences unrelated to the no-system-prompt baseline
the auditor could attempt to elicit the system prompt directly, only partially mitigated by an anti-leak instruction
the diffing agent is much better at identifying the correct behaviour than the correct trigger, though this might just be a property of the chosen triggers/behaviours

model organisms fine-tuned to exhibit a specific secret behaviour are not well described solely by their intended behaviour -- they come with other, sometimes more salient, differences from their base model
quote: diffing agents outperform standard auditing agents that only operate on a single model in cases where the behavioural change is subtle
